components.title: Working rules (CLAUDE.md block)
components.what: A before/during/after framework for every task (checkable criteria, a named bar, small verified steps, proof from real output, a self-check), plus token economy, a learning loop, session logs, cleanup, living docs and compaction instructions. Installed as one marked block; anything else in your CLAUDE.md stays.
pros: Finished, verified work instead of 'should work'
Claude decides routine choices and stops only for real forks
Lessons get saved once instead of re-taught
cons: About 3.6k tokens on every call (read from cache, so about 0.4k at full price)
Written in the first person for one owner: change the opening paragraph to your taste
Overlaps or conflicts with rules you already have

components.title: Auto-compact at 300k tokens
components.what: Sets CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=300000 and keeps auto-compaction on, so a long session compacts at about 268k.
pros: More working room before a compaction (a heavy setup starts near 80k and refills to ~110k after one)
Fewer compactions, each losing less
cons: Each call near the limit re-reads more context
Pointless on a model with a smaller window
components.cost: More tokens per call late in long sessions; fewer compactions

components.title: Tool search on
components.what: ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true: rarely used tools stay out of the prompt until searched for.
pros: Smaller prompt when many MCP servers or plugins are connected
Better tool choice past ~30 tools
cons: One extra search step the first time a deferred tool is needed
components.cost: Saves tokens when you have many tools

components.title: Subagents at medium effort
components.what: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT=medium: subagents think less than the main session.
pros: Subagent runs cost less and finish sooner
cons: Hard subagent tasks may need a higher effort set per agent

components.title: Concise output style
components.what: outputStyle=Concise: replies lead with the result, no narration or recaps.
pros: Shorter replies, less to read
Fewer output tokens (the most expensive kind)
cons: Less hand-holding; ask for detail when you want it

components.title: Keep transcripts 90 days
components.what: cleanupPeriodDays=90 instead of 30, so cache reports and past-session searches have history.
pros: Older sessions stay searchable and resumable
cons: Disk use: heavy users write gigabytes of transcripts a month

components.title: Auto-mode environment
components.what: Adds autoMode.environment with the built-in defaults, ready for your own lines (your organisation, protected branches, production services that need your yes).
pros: Auto mode judges risky actions with your context, not just generic rules
cons: Does nothing until you add your own lines

components.title: Deny reading secret files
components.what: Permission deny rules for ~/.ssh, .env and .env.local.
pros: Keys and passwords never enter the conversation
cons: You read those files yourself when needed

components.title: Ask before pushes and installs
components.what: Permission ask rules for git push, gh pr create, pip install, npm install -g and winget install.
pros: Nothing leaves your machine or lands on it without a yes
cons: One more prompt each time; drop it if you push many times a day
components.cost: A prompt per push or install

components.title: Status line with cache state
components.what: One line under the prompt (terminal): context used, whether the prompt cache is warm and for how many more minutes, hit rate and the last miss's cause.
pros: Shows when a break will cost a full re-cache
Spots cache-breaking changes as they happen
cons: Terminal only; replaces a status line you already have only if you have none

components.title: Shell guard + ratchet
components.what: PreToolUse hook on Bash and PowerShell. Denies commands touching .env, .env.local or ~/.ssh. Asks before pushes, installs, recursive deletes outside build and cache folders, git reset --hard, git clean, force-push, DROP TABLE, Docker prunes and disk formatting. On git commit it runs ratchet.mjs and asks when the diff passes by lowering the bar (new suppressions, skipped tests, stubs, fewer assertions, eased thresholds).
pros: Catches what permission rules miss when another hook rewrites commands
Stops the classic agent disasters (rm -rf, reset --hard) with a prompt, not after the fact
Stops 'tests pass' by skipping tests
cons: ~50 ms per shell command
Occasional prompt on a delete you meant
components.cost: No context; a node start per shell command

components.title: Edit boundary for parallel sessions
components.what: A message line 'EDIT-BOUNDARY: <folder>' fences that session's Edit and Write to the folder until 'EDIT-BOUNDARY: off'. For two sessions working in one repo.
pros: Parallel sessions can't overwrite each other's files
cons: Only useful if you run more than one session in a repo
A hook on every edit and prompt (~30 ms)
components.cost: No context; a node start per edit

components.title: Config change audit
components.what: Logs every change to a settings or skill file (which file, when, which session) to ~/.claude/logs/config-audit.log. Never blocks.
pros: A change you didn't make leaves a trace
cons: A log file that grows slowly

components.title: Session log guard
components.what: Stop hook: a turn that made 3+ changes can't end until a session-logs/*.md file was updated in that turn. Pairs with the session-log rule.
pros: Every step is written down, so compaction and restarts lose nothing
Makes the log rule automatic instead of hoped-for
cons: Claude spends a few tokens per turn writing the log
Pointless without the rules (or your own log habit)

components.title: Session resume after compaction + log compaction
components.what: Right after a compaction, puts the session's own log back into context, and nudges a lossless log compaction once the log passes 40 KB (log-compact.mjs archives it verbatim and checks no path, URL or ID was dropped).
pros: Compaction stops being the moment work gets lost
Logs stay small enough to re-read
cons: Re-reads the log's tail (up to ~10k tokens) after each compaction

components.title: Lead guard (desktop app, hub sessions)
components.what: Stop hook for a lead session that starts and coordinates other sessions in the Claude desktop app: it can't end a turn on a note from one of its sessions without sending the next step, archiving it, or writing 'No next step for <session>: <reason>'.
pros: Child sessions don't sit idle waiting for a lead that forgot them (before it: 10 of 71 'done' notes got a next step)
cons: Only for the desktop app's session tools; does nothing elsewhere
Finds children through the desktop session index; set LEAD_GUARD_SESSIONS_DIR if your app keeps it elsewhere
components.cost: No context; reads the transcript tail at each stop

components.title: cache-report.py
components.what: Reads local transcripts and reports prompt-cache hit rate, weighted spend shares, why the cache was rewritten and which sessions cost the most. Needs Python 3.
pros: Shows where tokens actually go before you optimise anything
cons: Needs Python

components.title: reddit.py
components.what: Read Reddit for research: top, search, thread, through the public Arctic Shift archive (or the official API with your own app keys). Needs Python 3.
pros: Works where browser tools and web search can't reach Reddit
cons: Archive data lags live Reddit slightly

components.title: grilling
components.what: Interviews you relentlessly about a plan until every branch of the decision tree is settled.
pros: Big or fuzzy jobs start from a shared, specific plan
cons: ~60 tokens of description in every session

components.title: human-voice
components.what: Writing that reads like one sharp, warm person: point first, specifics, earned wit, plus slop_check.py and quote_check.py scripts that flag AI tells.
pros: Emails, posts and docs that don't read as AI
Mechanical checks, not just advice
cons: ~120 tokens of description in every session
Opinionated style

components.title: gauntlet-loop
components.what: Holds work to a real, named reference with blind critics until ours wins, or a metric mode for jobs with a hard number. Only runs when you type /gauntlet-loop.
pros: The strongest quality loop for work that must beat a known bar
cons: Runs subagents: expensive, so it's user-invoked only

components.title: after-restart (Windows)
components.what: After a PC restart, crash or app freeze: finds the cause in the Windows event logs and resumes the sessions that were mid-task.
pros: Turns a crash into a five-minute recovery
cons: Windows only (PowerShell event logs)

components.title: smart-compact mod
components.what: A Claude Code mod (plugin). 55 minutes into an idle gap, if context is over 200k, it compacts while the 1-hour prompt cache is still warm, so the next message rewrites ~110k instead of 220k+ (the desktop app has no idle compaction of its own). Also gives the model a compact_after_turn tool for finished-task boundaries over 150k.
pros: Cuts the biggest cache-write cost of long-lived sessions (cold wakes were ~40% of cache writes in our data)
cons: Compaction drops detail (the session log and Compact instructions limit that)
A compaction is wasted if you never come back to that session
components.cost: One summary over a warm cache per idle gap over 200k

components.title: email-shield mod
components.what: Removes the account email Claude Code adds to every prompt (anthropics/claude-code#81138) and blocks any outbound tool call whose input carries it.
pros: Your login email never reaches a web request, MCP server or subagent
cons: Only matters if your account email shows up in prompts (claude.ai login)
